results.title: The best Loom alternatives in 2026 | Supercut
results.content:
You still want what Loom does well: record your screen and camera, send a link fast, do a bit of editing, and use AI workflows to turn a video into docs, issues and messages, or record it for an AI agent to work from.

Which tool fits best depends on what you care about most. Each one is doubling down on something different: some on quick sharing and turning videos into work, others on editing. So we grouped them that way, because no tool is best at both... yet!

At a glance [...] Supercut is built so anyone on the team can use it, not only engineers. The Mac and Windows apps record your screen and camera separately, so videos look composed and on brand, you can change the layout after recording, and the link is ready the moment you stop. Every video comes with a summary, chapters, a transcript and an AI assistant viewers can ask, and viewers are free on every plan. Agents are just as easy to set up: the Supercut MCP is a connector in Claude’s directory, so you add it [...] It is pushing toward agents too.Its MCP server lets an AI assistant read a Zight video’s recording, transcript, on-screen text and any console logs collected with it, and create Request Links that ask someone else to record their screen. Its Playbooks, in limited beta, turn a recorded browser task into steps an agent can run.

results.title: The Best Loom Alternatives by Use Case
results.content:
The difference starts with what AI actually does. Loom’s AI generates titles and descriptions after a rep has already done the work of recording. Vidyard’s AI generates entire videos meaning a rep who would have spent 20 minutes recording, reviewing, and sending a personalized message now spends zero. Multiply that across 50 prospects a week and the productivity gap becomes a pipeline gap. [...] Every tool now offers auto-generated titles and summaries, but only some can generate videos on your behalf or trigger automated outreach based on buyer behavior. Loom’s AI features center on auto-generated titles and descriptions for recorded videos. That’s table stakes. The question is what AI does after the recording, or whether it can eliminate the recording altogether.

### Integration depth with your existing systems [...] For teams that still want to record manually, Video Messages covers that ground. The Chrome extension captures screen and webcam recordings with in-video CTAs, AI-assisted scripts, and the same viewer-level analytics. Manual recording and AI-generated videos coexist on the same platform, which means a rep can send a hand-recorded walkthrough for a high-value deal and let Video Agent handle the rest.

results.title: Introducing Clips: An open-source, agent-native Loom alternative
results.content:
Instead, I have a hotkey. Whenever something goes wrong, I hit it, start talking, point at the problem, and get a link to send to my agent.

It reads what I said, looks at the screen where I pointed, and, if it was a browser tab, checks the logs. Then it fixes the thing, or answers me in a comment on the clip.

Clips is our open-source Loom alternative, built so every recording is something your agent can watch. And it still does everything you'd use Loom for. Today it's in beta. [...] ## Your agent can answer on the clip

A clip doesn't have to be a one-way handoff. People can comment on a moment, react, mention a teammate, and reply in threads, so the conversation about a recording happens on the recording.

Agents can join in. Connect your agent to Clips through its MCP server, a standard way to give an agent an app's tools, and it can read a clip's comments and reply in the thread, set chapters, or upload a video of its own and get the share link back. [...] Copying software is cheap now. Making it good isn't. Anyone can point an agent at Loom and get a clone, but as I wrote a couple of weeks ago, the best a clone can do is tie. Loom now has a recording mode for agents on its paid plans. We'd rather make every clip work with your agent, for free, keep it MIT-licensed, and take the best fixes back upstream so everyone gets them.
